On Tue, 30 Sep 2026 19:02 +1100 Samantha Ng wrote:
> Quick clarification — the Option A time (Oct 1, 12:00 AEDT) shows on our calendar as Oct 1 which is fine, but Tom and I just noticed that one of our execs is in Tokyo and their calendar is tagging the event on their calendar as Oct 2 (transition at midnight).

Thanks for the note, Samantha — happy to clear this up. Two quick things that cause the "next day" label:

1) Local date vs UTC conversion: If the calendar event is created in UTC and a client (Outlook/Google) displays the local date after applying offset, it can appear as previous/next day depending on the offset.
2) DST / zone naming mismatch: Sydney is at UTC+11 (AEDT) while Tokyo is UTC+9 (JST). A 00:30 UTC event falls on different local dates for each zone, so an invite created in one zone without explicit local-time metadata can be ambiguous.

If we lock the invite to "Asia/Singapore" (SGT; UTC+8) and explicitly list local times in the description, it avoids most client oddities. Given the team's preferences, my recommendation:

- Move to Fri Oct 2, 11:00 AEDT (Fri Oct 2, 10:00 SGT / Fri Oct 2, 09:00 JST) as Samantha proposed.
- I'll ask our solutions engineer to join for the Fri slot.
- Mateo — please resend the invite with zone set to Asia/Singapore and include the local-time table in the body + an ICS that explicitly sets DTSTART/DTEND with TZID=Asia/Singapore.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
